# SEAM by Kiwe

> Canonical command boundary for attachment-aware website ideation, auditing, fixing and WordPress binding preparation.

- [Start contract](https://start.kiwelaunch.com/start.md)
- [Command manifest](https://start.kiwelaunch.com/command-manifest.json)
- [Machine registry](https://start.kiwelaunch.com/.well-known/kiwe.json)
- [GitHub source mirror](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Museintel/kiwe/codex/phonekey-whatsapp-rc1/KIWE-START.md)

Never substitute kiwilaunch.com or another similarly named domain.

---

# SEAM Start

Contract version: `8.7`
Updated: `2026-08-26`

Read the matching [canonical command manifest](https://start.kiwelaunch.com/command-manifest.json) before acting. If the canonical host is unavailable to the participating AI, read the [GitHub manifest mirror](https://github.com/Museintel/kiwe/blob/codex/phonekey-whatsapp-rc1/kiwe-ai-toolkit/command-manifest.json) and the linked GitHub command context instead. Do not crawl the repository, substitute a similarly named domain, or use a command remembered from an older conversation.

Inspect supplied attachments even when the user gives only this start link. If no slash command is present, identify each attachment by content rather than filename, recommend exactly one of the six commands with a one-sentence reason, and wait for that command. Do not silently execute a guessed command. A raw HTML/CSS/JS project needing design work normally suggests `/ideate`; an accepted raw project needing WordPress binding intent suggests `/convert /bricks`; an artifact needing inspection suggests `/audit` or `/accessibility`; a report with proven findings suggests `/fix`; and a failed generated output suggests `/redo`.

SEAM has six commands:

- [`/ideate`](https://start.kiwelaunch.com/contexts/ideate.md) ([GitHub context mirror](https://github.com/Museintel/kiwe/blob/codex/phonekey-whatsapp-rc1/kiwe-ai-toolkit/contexts/ideate.md)) — inspect the supplied project, establish whether its design is final, enhancement-authorized or redesign-authorized, classify whether SiteGraph is required, report Design Context coverage, then create or refine raw HTML/CSS/JS without imposing a house style.
- [`/convert /bricks`](https://start.kiwelaunch.com/contexts/convert-bricks.md) ([GitHub context mirror](https://github.com/Museintel/kiwe/blob/codex/phonekey-whatsapp-rc1/kiwe-ai-toolkit/contexts/convert-bricks.md)) — prepare both Bricks dynamic tags and query-loop bindings; add `/dynamictags` or `/queryloop` to request only one binding type.
- [`/audit`](https://start.kiwelaunch.com/contexts/audit.md) ([GitHub context mirror](https://github.com/Museintel/kiwe/blob/codex/phonekey-whatsapp-rc1/kiwe-ai-toolkit/contexts/audit.md)) — inspect an artifact without changing it.
- [`/accessibility`](https://start.kiwelaunch.com/contexts/accessibility.md) ([GitHub context mirror](https://github.com/Museintel/kiwe/blob/codex/phonekey-whatsapp-rc1/kiwe-ai-toolkit/contexts/accessibility.md)) — audit accessibility, responsive geometry and light/dark presentation.
- [`/fix`](https://start.kiwelaunch.com/contexts/accessibility.md) ([GitHub context mirror](https://github.com/Museintel/kiwe/blob/codex/phonekey-whatsapp-rc1/kiwe-ai-toolkit/contexts/accessibility.md)) — correct proven audit findings while preserving the accepted design.
- [`/redo`](https://start.kiwelaunch.com/contexts/audit.md) ([GitHub context mirror](https://github.com/Museintel/kiwe/blob/codex/phonekey-whatsapp-rc1/kiwe-ai-toolkit/contexts/audit.md)) — replace a failed output from the last accepted artifact and failure evidence.

SiteGraph and its embedded Design Context are attached or safely connected project inputs. They are not commands. For an existing supplied design, `/ideate` first establishes source authority: final/approved, enhancement-authorized, or redesign-authorized. The command itself never grants redesign permission. If the user's intent is not explicit, the AI asks that one question and stops. It then classifies SiteGraph as required, beneficial or not needed. If required evidence is absent, it asks for one safe read-only handoff. Attaching or connecting that requested evidence never counts as `proceed`: the AI must next report Design Context coverage and a concise, page-relevant Design Context and Design Content usage brief, stop, and wait for the user's explicit `proceed` before changing or creating files. Seam Framework is an explicit `seam.kiwe` compiler option, not a separate command. Browser AI never emits production Bricks JSON; only the `seam.kiwe` application does.

Unknown commands, aliases and unsupported modifiers must be rejected.

--- /ideate ---

# /ideate

Start with discovery, not a fixed questionnaire. Inspect every supplied file by its contents before asking anything. Treat the attachments themselves as the source brief; do not ask the user to describe files that can be inspected.

For any supplied existing design, establish its **source authority before choosing a creative lane**. Resolve exactly one of: `approved-final`, `enhancement-authorized`, or `redesign-authorized`. Only an explicit user statement can authorize enhancement or redesign; `/ideate`, the presence of source files, visual defects, stale navigation, missing content, or the AI's preference never grants that authority. If the conversation does not prove the answer, ask exactly one question: **“Is this design final/approved, should I enhance it without changing its art direction, or are you asking for a redesign?”** Then stop. Do not select a direction, propose an art style, request SiteGraph, emit a usage brief, or create files until the user answers. If the user says only “final” or “approved,” treat that as `approved-final`.

After source authority is resolved, determine the proven lane: a new website, preservation of an approved existing design, enhancement/expansion without changing its accepted art direction, or an explicitly authorized redesign. State the detected lane and ask only for another missing decision when it materially changes the result. Never ask again for facts already supplied by the project, SiteGraph or its embedded Design Context.

Once source authority is resolved, classify SiteGraph as `required`, `beneficial`, or `not-needed` and explain the evidence. SiteGraph is required when the requested result must use or preserve real site identity, owner decisions, media, products, posts, services, menus, taxonomies, custom fields, commerce data, or future dynamic-binding intent that the supplied files do not prove completely. It is beneficial but optional for an ungrounded concept that may use honest placeholders. It is not needed when the approved supplied project is self-contained and the requested work neither introduces nor changes site-owned facts. If required evidence is absent, stop before recreation and request exactly one safe SiteGraph handoff.

Choose the safest SiteGraph connection the participating AI can actually use. Prefer an already connected read-only SiteGraph tool or MCP resource; otherwise use a scoped, expiring task-capsule/API connection; otherwise request an attached current SiteGraph export. Do not pretend an unavailable connector worked, ask the user to choose technical transport, request a broad permanent key, or paste secrets into project output. Explain the one action required only when no safe connection is available.

Inventory approved source pages, assets, references and existing-site evidence before proposing work. Existing Design Context is authoritative for business facts and owner-locked brand values; SiteGraph design content supplies real media, products, posts, taxonomies, custom content and public identity. Distinguish read-only owner facts from AI-writable suggestions.

When SiteGraph is present, report **Design Context coverage before changing any file**. Use `seamDesignContext.scores.designContextStrength` as the authoritative percentage when supplied. Otherwise calculate coverage—not subjective design quality—using this evidence rubric: identity 15%, audience and goal 10%, brand preferences 15%, public contact and localization 10%, about/founder/team 15%, pages/services/content plan 10%, commerce and product context 15%, and approved resources/media 10%. Exclude a genuinely irrelevant section and redistribute its weight proportionally; never award points for guessed values or placeholders. Show the percentage, covered sections, material gaps, locked owner facts, preserved owner preferences, AI-writable gaps, and the SiteGraph/context hash when available. If SiteGraph is not needed, record coverage as `not-applicable` rather than fabricating a number.

Next share a concise **usage brief** before changing any file. Under Design Context, list only the verified owner facts and preferences that will materially affect this requested page or project. Under Design Content, shortlist only the real products, posts, services, menus and media that have a clear intended role in the proposed result. Select media by semantic metadata, intended resource role, orientation/aspect ratio and the actual section need; do not enumerate, download or force every SiteGraph media item into the design. State what will remain dynamic, what is preview evidence only, and any ambiguity requiring review.

Perform a **production-content readiness preflight** as part of that brief. When the user requests a final, production-ready or approved project and SiteGraph or the supplied self-contained source proves sufficient business context, every visible content region must contain grounded, page-appropriate final copy, a proven dynamic-binding intent, or an explicit human-review item. Do not leave lorem ipsum, “sample”, “dummy”, “placeholder”, TODO text, repeated generic filler, invented testimonials, fake statistics, guessed prices, unproven certifications, unsupported claims or fabricated contact/legal/compliance facts. Use verified SiteGraph facts and the page's purpose to complete the copy without changing an approved composition, hierarchy or art direction. Do not keyword-stuff. Preview placeholders are allowed only for an explicitly ungrounded concept where SiteGraph is not required; identify every such region in the discovery artifact and never represent that artifact as production-ready. If required facts are unavailable, mark the affected region blocked rather than guessing.

Then stop and ask the user to say `proceed`. Providing, attaching, replacing, reconnecting or updating SiteGraph, Design Context, source files, references or assets only satisfies an input request; it is never approval, never means `proceed`, and never authorizes file generation. After receiving any requested SiteGraph or other evidence, read it, emit the coverage report, usage brief and content-readiness preflight, and stop again. Do not create or modify output files before that explicit response. The explicit response must occur after the usage brief. Emit `ideate/kiwe-ideate-discovery.json` using schema `kiwe.ideate-discovery.v5` with approval status `awaiting-user` during this pause. After `proceed`, set it to `approved`, preserve the approved source authority and usage brief as the implementation boundary, and produce the project without another generic questionnaire. A later material change to either boundary requires a new approval; small conversational corrections do not.

Do not apply Seam Framework, Bricks structures or a SEAM house style. Do not flatten unusual but intentional art direction into a component library. Keep corrections conversational until the user accepts the result.

Return a complete browser-runnable HTML/CSS/JS project appropriate to the detected lane: create a coherent new project, preserve an approved existing design, enhance it within its accepted art direction, or redesign it only when explicitly authorized. For `approved-final`, visual composition, palette, typography, spacing system, responsive behavior, content hierarchy, page boundaries and JavaScript are immutable except for explicit user corrections; SiteGraph may ground content, media and functional intent and may add non-visual semantic/dynamic markers. Never collapse multiple supplied pages into one JavaScript-switched document unless the user explicitly requests a single-file application. When a single-file application is supplied or explicitly requested, give each page view a stable unique `data-view`, `data-page`, or `data-route-view` marker so `seam.kiwe` can partition shared header/footer and page bodies deterministically. Include every required local asset and `assets/asset-manifest.json`, recording provenance and intended WordPress Media use. Preserve semantic regions and add stable `data-seam-role` markers only when they clarify meaning without changing presentation. Mark dynamic intent such as product title, price, media, contact data or repeated collections when SiteGraph proves the binding. Never invent IDs, fields, products or site facts. Before delivery, load every entry page at its intended desktop and mobile viewport and fail closed on uncaught JavaScript errors, missing-selector initialization, empty required regions, broken local links, missing required assets, or unintended document overflow. Bind scripts only to elements that exist. Record the runtime result in `contentReadiness.runtimeSmokeTest`; an artifact that fails this check is not production-ready.


--- /convert /bricks ---

# /convert /bricks

This is the browser-AI preparation lane, not the JSON compiler. Its input is the complete accepted HTML/CSS/JS project plus assets and, whenever real site fields are requested, a current SiteGraph connection or export.

Preserve the rendered source, responsive behavior, content and JavaScript. Add stable unique source selectors only where required to describe Bricks binding intent. By default, identify both singular dynamic fields and repeated query regions. `/convert /bricks /dynamictags` limits the pass to singular dynamic text, links, images and supported WooCommerce fields. `/convert /bricks /queryloop` limits the pass to repeated Bricks query-loop regions. The modifiers are mutually exclusive and never change visual design.

Use only post types, taxonomies, term IDs, fields, dynamic tags and query object types proven by SiteGraph or the public Bricks contract. Never invent a site-specific ID or field. Preserve static preview content but mark production regions as dynamic. Record launchers for proven Kiwe capabilities without replacing source popups or interactions that have distinct intent.

Return the complete updated raw project, `bricks-bindings/kiwe-bindings.json` using schema `kiwe.bricks-bindings.v1`, and a binding report covering `queries`, `dynamicFields`, `launchers`, `menuContext`, `assumptions` and `requiresHumanReview`. Do not emit a Bricks template, Bricks JSON, Framework Profile or compiler confidence score. The user submits this package to `seam.kiwe`, whose deterministic compiler alone produces and validates native Bricks JSON.


--- /audit ---

# /audit and /redo

Audit is read-only. Inspect the supplied artifact against its accepted source, declared contract and available rendered evidence. Report concrete findings with severity, selector or element ID, breakpoint, expected result, observed result and evidence. Scores must be reproducible from findings, not intuition.

For `/redo`, treat the last accepted artifact as authority and the failed output only as evidence. Re-run the responsible stage, close each proven failure and report unresolved items. Do not stack speculative patches on top of the failed artifact and do not redesign unrelated areas.


--- /accessibility ---

# /accessibility and /fix

Audit accessibility and visual robustness across keyboard use, focus, landmarks, names, headings, labels, reduced motion, contrast, readable text, overflow, clipping, collision, touch targets, responsive spacing, alignment and light/dark presentation. Distinguish source defects from conversion defects.

Dark mode must preserve brand identity and visual hierarchy, not turn every surface black. Keep owner-locked brand colors, derive accessible supporting surfaces deliberately, and test foreground/background pairs in their actual states. Decorative text and imagery must remain decorative; do not promote low-opacity or layered art into primary readable content.

`/accessibility` produces evidence and a report without changing the artifact. `/fix` applies only proven findings, preserves accepted art direction and behavior, then re-runs the same checks and returns before/after scores. Prefer native Bricks settings for Bricks artifacts and native CSS/HTML semantics for raw projects. Flag what cannot be fixed safely instead of guessing.


--- /fix ---

# /accessibility and /fix

Audit accessibility and visual robustness across keyboard use, focus, landmarks, names, headings, labels, reduced motion, contrast, readable text, overflow, clipping, collision, touch targets, responsive spacing, alignment and light/dark presentation. Distinguish source defects from conversion defects.

Dark mode must preserve brand identity and visual hierarchy, not turn every surface black. Keep owner-locked brand colors, derive accessible supporting surfaces deliberately, and test foreground/background pairs in their actual states. Decorative text and imagery must remain decorative; do not promote low-opacity or layered art into primary readable content.

`/accessibility` produces evidence and a report without changing the artifact. `/fix` applies only proven findings, preserves accepted art direction and behavior, then re-runs the same checks and returns before/after scores. Prefer native Bricks settings for Bricks artifacts and native CSS/HTML semantics for raw projects. Flag what cannot be fixed safely instead of guessing.
